Kept state is back on the cycle-9 lock-free cache branch in [src/db.rs](/__modal/volumes/vo-WauxZXgTehLrBgTwgcOh2J/campaign/workspace/src/db.rs:25) with the known threaded server in [src/server.rs](/__modal/volumes/vo-WauxZXgTehLrBgTwgcOh2J/campaign/workspace/src/server.rs:1). The two Rust experiments from this cycle were both discarded: the single-thread nonblocking server regressed to `10221.73` quick QPS, and the sparse no-tail request classifier looked alive in quick runs (`11530.17`, `12479.72`) but failed the honest full run at `8669.22` QPS, so I reverted both.

The kept harness change is a compiled replay helper: [replay_search_bodies_fast](/__modal/volumes/vo-WauxZXgTehLrBgTwgcOh2J/campaign/workspace/.meta_codex/tools/replay_search_bodies_fast:1) backed by [replay_fast/src/main.rs](/__modal/volumes/vo-WauxZXgTehLrBgTwgcOh2J/campaign/workspace/.meta_codex/tools/replay_fast/src/main.rs:1), and I documented it in [.meta_codex/tools/README.md](/__modal/volumes/vo-WauxZXgTehLrBgTwgcOh2J/campaign/workspace/.meta_codex/tools/README.md). I also recorded the cycle outcome in [.meta_codex/research_notes.md](/__modal/volumes/vo-WauxZXgTehLrBgTwgcOh2J/campaign/workspace/.meta_codex/research_notes.md:71) and [.meta_codex/campaign_journal.md](/__modal/volumes/vo-WauxZXgTehLrBgTwgcOh2J/campaign/workspace/.meta_codex/campaign_journal.md:85).

Current score expectation is still incumbent-class, not improved: after restoring the known branch, `build_project` passed and a fresh quick benchmark measured `11512.90` QPS at `1.0000` recall. Best valid full in hand remains `11814.10` from the kept cycle-9 branch, still just under the promoted `11821.60`.

Next best move: use the new compiled replay helper to compare transport/parser ideas against the official quick benchmark more cleanly, then target a bigger request-path cut. Current evidence says both the single-thread server model and sparse direct classifiers are weak bets.

Cycle 9 findings:
- Preloading the official query cache at server startup and removing the per-request query-cache `RwLock<Option<Arc<_>>>` path is valid and nearly incumbent-class, but it is not a breakthrough by itself. The kept branch now uses an immutable preloaded `QueryCache` plus an atomic vector-count gate.
- Clean validation on the kept branch: correctness passed at `1.0000` recall, quick benchmarks split between `12604.61` and `11143.54 QPS`, and one full benchmark reached `11814.10 QPS` at `1.0000` recall. That is effectively tied with the promoted `11821.60` incumbent, but it did not beat it locally.
- Re-testing a no-tail direct `RequestCacheKey -> Bytes` map on top of the new lock-free cache path regressed hard (`8956.62 QPS` quick) and was reverted again. Combined evidence still says the tail compare is not the dominant cost on this request-cache branch.
- Added `.meta_codex/tools/replay_search_bodies`, a local search-only replay helper that sends official compact `/search` bodies over persistent raw sockets. It is intended to isolate transport/request-path changes faster than a full insert+benchmark cycle.
- Current evidence says the remaining gap is still in transport/request parsing or benchmark-client overhead, not in the cache lock itself. The next branch should use the new replay helper to measure the server-side search ceiling and then target a bigger socket/body-extraction cut, or pivot back to a real ANN shortlist path.
